questions.ask: What are the last four digits of your account number?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions financial hardship: job loss, illness, bereavement, being unable to afford essentials.
intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague time such as "soon" or "after payday".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.
intents.human: A request to speak to a human.

lines.opening: Good day, this is Isla, Corran Bank's automated assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: To check, please call the number on the back of your card.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only explain once I know I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only arrange a call on a business day, today or in the next two business days, between 9:30 in the morning and 6 in the evening. Could you suggest another time?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {first_name} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have bothered you.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_explain: I can only continue once both questions are answered.
lines.id_declined: I'm sorry, I can't continue without those answers.
lines.id_repeat: Could you say that again, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our details.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I could not confirm your identity. Please call the number on the back of your card or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, the lowest amount I can accept is {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Which date from today would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That is not a business day. The next date I can offer is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay by {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Could you give me an exact date?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can use is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a confirmation by text message.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, because of a system problem your promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment today.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'll put you through to our care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to a colleague who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with first?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change the promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book that call.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

assumptions: The brief's opening says 'This call is recorded.' The spec format says to use the active voice 'We record this call' and allows the word 'recorded' only in the recorded, sms_line and record_failed lines. The opening is changed to match; the rest of the brief's wording is kept.
The brief does not say how 'next <weekday>' is read. The default 'following_week' is used.

Callbacks (rule 5) may be booked only on a business day: today if it is a business day, or one of the next two business days. Times run from 09:30 to 18:00, both ends included, and must be later than now. A bad slot gets one more ask, so max_asks is 2 (rule 6).

Identity: two questions in order, postcode then account_last4. Two wrong answers in total end the check, so max_wrong is 2 (rule 11 and the API summary). The postcode is sent in capitals with every space removed, so no space format is set. The postcode has no fixed length. account_last4 is exactly 4 digits with leading zeros kept.

The verify_identity response has no hint field (only ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified), so identity.response has no hint key and hints is empty. date_order 'dmy' is a default that is not used, since no question asks for a date.

Refusing to answer: the agent explains once that the questions protect the account. A second refusal means identity is declined (rule 12). Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as a refusal (default kept).
get_account returns amounts in pounds (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes whole pence, so promise_scale is 100: £85.50 becomes 8550.

Floor (rule 22): minimum_due for credit_card and overdraft, monthly_instalment for personal_loan. If that field is higher than past_due, the floor is min(field, past_due). The brief gives no rounding, so amounts are used as given (floor_round null). Every proposal that uses the floor uses this clamped value.
Early band, days 1 to 10: the deadline is the 8th business day after today, and today does not count. Attempts: 1.

Middle band, days 11 to 30: the deadline is today plus 14 calendar days. If that is a non-business day it moves forward to the next business day, which is why deadline_adjust is next_business_day. Attempts: 2.

Late band, days 31 to 60: the deadline is the last business day of the current month. If that is earlier than today, the last business day of next month is used. If it equals today, today stays the deadline, so roll_if_not_after_today is false. Example: now 2026-11-28 to 2026-11-30 gives 2026-11-27, which has passed, so the deadline rolls to 2026-12-30 (2026-12-31 is a holiday). Attempts: 3.

Ladder (rule 26). Attempt 1: past_due on the next business day, or on the deadline if that is earlier. Middle attempt 2: the floor on the deadline. Late attempt 2: past_due on the deadline. Late attempt 3: the floor on the deadline. Steps that use past_due are full_or_floor, because after 'too much' every proposal uses the floor (rule 24). The engine is assumed to clamp proposal dates to the deadline.

Rule 27: a step that would exactly repeat an earlier proposal is skipped and the customer is not asked again. For example, in the late band, when the deadline is the next business day, attempt 2 equals attempt 1. After 'too much', late attempts 2 and 3 are also identical. When the ladder is used up, the customer has refused (rule 29).

The first ask is 'Can you pay the full amount today?'. It is not an attempt (rule 25), so the attempt counts are follow-on proposals only. If the customer says the full amount is too much, the floor is offered once on the date of the current proposal and uses no attempt (too_much_floor asked_date). Refusing the floor is a flat refusal.
Rule 24: below the floor, the agent says it cannot be recorded and offers the floor once.
Rule 21: a vague date gets one request for an exact date. If none follows, it is a flat refusal.
Hardship (rule 37) transfers straight to the 'care' queue with outcome transferred / hardship and no note. transfer_support uses the same values.
Notes are enabled. Only already paid (claims_paid), refused (customer_refused), dispute (disputed) and system failure (system_failure) get add_note, just before close_call.
The brief does not say whether to ask 'anything else' after a recorded promise. The default true is used.
The brief does not say how many 'I don't want to talk' replies end the call. The default 2 is used.
The brief does not say whether a recorded promise can be changed, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
Rule 33: a failed create_promise is retried once. A second failure is a system failure.
There is one product per call, so the multi-product settings keep their defaults and do not apply.
The brief covers days late 1 to 60 and gives no rule for values outside, so bands_outside is null.
Every tool's success flag is ok: true, from the tool API's response schema.
